column15: Verified owner (Asahi Group Holdings) and structure via Wikipedia (opened): Yoichi (peated-style, maritime) + Miyagikyo (unpeated, lighter) distilleries plus Ben Nevis in Scotland (acquired 1989). Corrected defaultTypeName from blend to empty: samples span blend (Nikka, From The Barrel), single grain (Coffey Grain) and single malt via continuous still (Coffey Malt), not only blend. Peat kept unknown: Yoichi malt proportion is undisclosed per expression and Coffey Grain has no malt at all, so no single level applies across the row's samples.

Confirmed Hombo Shuzo ownership (Wikipedia, opened) and the four barley peating levels used across releases - unpeated, lightly peated 3.5ppm, heavily peated 20ppm, super-heavily peated 50ppm (distilando.com, opened) - at both Shinshu and Tsunuki distilleries; Shinshu malt also feeds the Maltage Cosmo and Kasei blends. Peat kept unknown for this umbrella row since no single level applies; samples span both distilleries and several product lines (Iwai/Kasei/Cosmo/Tsunuki/Y.A).

Official site is reachable this session (the seed reported it unreachable/lapsed) - confirms Scotland-based (Dumfries House Estate, Ayrshire), a blending house that recreates historic distillery flavour profiles from aged single malts, self-operated with no separate parent company found. Peat kept unknown: the site's own regional lines vary sharply (Lossit/Islay markets 'Smoked Almond & Pear'; Towiemore/Speyside markets 'Green Apple & Cake'), confirming the seed's reasoning that one peat value would misrepresent the range. A human split into per-release rows (Lossit, Towiemore, Stratheden, Dalaruan/Jericho, Gerston) remains worth doing but is beyond this round's scope.

Confirmed via MGP's own page (opened): Niche Drinks (Derry, Northern Ireland) is described as 'Luxco's Irish extension', and MGP Ingredients now owns Luxco. No peat mentioned anywhere. countryCode kept IE per the seed's documented convention (the product is marketed/sold under the Irish whiskey geographic category) though Derry is politically in the UK. Range spans a blend and an 8-year single malt, so defaultTypeName stays empty.

column7: CVH Spirits (Capevin Holdings; formerly Burn Stewart Distillers / Distell International)
column15: CORRECTED owner from Distell Group: Heineken acquired most of Distell Group in 2023; the Scotch whisky business (formerly Burn Stewart Distillers) was spun out under Capevin Holdings (59.5% owned by Remgro) and renamed CVH Spirits on 27 April 2023. CVH's own site (opened) confirms it now owns Scottish Leader plus Black Bottle and the Bunnahabhain/Deanston/Tobermory/Ledaig distilleries. Peat kept none: CVH's own sibling blend Black Bottle is the one marketed as 'Islay-influenced', implying Scottish Leader is the non-smoky mainstream blend in the same portfolio, though no explicit 'unpeated' statement for Scottish Leader itself was found.

column7: Maison des Futailles (now Station 22, majority-owned by the Dandurand Group since 2022)
column15: Confirmed via opened sources that Maison des Futailles (Montreal/Boucherville, Quebec, founded 1922) rebranded to Station 22 in March 2022 and is now majority-owned by the Dandurand Group after Kruger sold its stake; retailers still market the product as 'Maison Des Futailles Spicebox'. Canadian spiced/flavored whisky (Cinnamon, Pumpkin, Ginger Bread, Chocolat editions); no peat mentioned in any source found for this or any sibling edition.

column7: Minami Alps Wine & Beverage Co., Ltd.
column15: Identified and confirmed the producer, previously blank in the seed row: Minami Alps Wine & Beverage Co., Ltd. (a subsidiary of Tokuoka Co., Ltd., established 2012), based in Fuefuki, Yamanashi Prefecture near Mt Fuji; master blender Kenji Watanabe. Peat kept unknown: some reviews mention 'a light hint of peat' or a 'sweet smoky aroma', which reads as tasting-note language rather than a stated peated-malt component, and no producer-domain statement either way was found (tenjakuwhisky.co.uk and tenjakuwhiskyusa.com, both opened, are silent on peat/smoke as a specified ingredient).

Confirmed real Swedish single malt distillery in Arboga via its own domain (agitatordistillery.com, opened). Added defaultTypeName=single malt (the whole range - base, Rok/Rok, Argument series - is single malt whisky; no grain or blended product found). REVIEWER FLAG RESOLVED: 'Agitator Rok' is real and matches 'Rok' (Swedish for smoke) on the official site, which IS a smoky/peated expression - confirmed on the producer's own product page (opened): 'a smooth smokey single malt whisky' with 'flattering peaty notes', matured in ex-Islay and chestnut casks. Wrote a peat rule for pattern 'rok' (peatProfile=light, per independent reviews calling it mild/'far from Islay-level' smoke) - see rule.tsv. The umbrella row's peat stays unknown: whiskynotes.be documents both an unpeated 2019 release and a peated 2020 release under the plain 'Agitator' name, so no single level applies to the base range either.

No distillery of this name in Scotland, consistent with the seed. Multiple retailer/registry listings (whiskybase, a ProWein trademark listing, winestyleonline) title it 'Glendale Blended Scotch Whisky', and one real independent blender/bottler, Campbell Meyer & Company Ltd (East Kilbride/Glasgow - confirmed real via campbellmeyer.com, opened, which describes exactly this kind of own-label blending/bottling business), surfaced repeatedly in search results as its likely bottler. I could not open a page this session that names Campbell Meyer as Glendale's bottler specifically (campbellmeyer.com itself did not list its brand roster; iwsc.net and whiskybase.com both returned 403), so owner is left blank and confidence stays low pending a source I can actually open. Treated as a generic own-label Scotch blend; no peat evidence found in any source.

CORRECTED: confirmed via caskcartel.com (opened) that Highland Baron is 'Made at Loch Lomond Distillery', blended from grain and Highland single malt whisky. Search results (an IWSC listing titled 'Loch Lomond Group | Highland Baron...', other retailers) additionally tie it to export house Mackay & McDavitt Co. for the Spanish market, but I could not open a page confirming that bottler relationship directly this session (iwsc.net, whiskybase.com and cgarsltd.co.uk all returned 403/406), so owner records only the confirmed production-site fact. Peat DOWNGRADED from the seed's none to unknown: one retailer description (not opened, search-synthesis only) mentions 'a delicate peat finish'; withheld peat proposal: light, uncorroborated by any producer-domain source, so kept unknown per policy rather than asserted either way. Catalogue carries both the typo 'Highiland Baron' and the correct 'Highland Baron' spelling.

Confirmed via Whyte & Mackay's own brand page (opened): range is Finest plus Reserve (Highland malt + Speyside malt + grain, 40 components, double sherry-cask maturation for Reserve), blended by Richard Paterson. CORRECTED peat from the seed's none to unknown: the official page makes no peat statement either way, while independent reviews (The Scotch Noob and others, not producer-confirmed) describe John Barr Reserve specifically with 'a stream of tangy peat at the finish' and 'a subtle wisp of peat smoke', so a blanket unpeated claim covering the whole row (which includes Reserve) is not safe. Withheld peat proposal: light for Reserve specifically, per uncorroborated third-party reviews only.

Confirmed via siredwards.com (own site, opened): 'Product of Scotland', range = Finest / Smoky / Beer Reserve / Aged 12 Years. Confirmed via la-martiniquaise.com (opened) that La Martiniquaise owns Sir Edward's, listed among its 'millionaire brands' alongside Label 5 - this resolves the seed's caveat that the owner was not independently re-confirmed. 'Finest' (catalogued here as 'Sir Edwards Finests', a typo) is the unpeated base; see rule.tsv for the separately-named 'Smoky' line, independently confirmed peated via its own producer-domain page.

Confirmed via globalnews.ca (opened): own distillery in Lethbridge, Alberta; Heaven Hill Brands purchased it effective 1 November 2019 (from Constellation Brands). No peat mentioned; Canadian whisky has no peat tradition. defaultTypeName kept empty - Canadian blended whisky has no clean match in the closed type list.

Confirmed via distillerytrail.com (opened): Coalition Whiskey is 'distilled, aged and bottled at Kentucky Artisan Distillery' in Crestwood, KY (pre-Prohibition all-copper pot still, zero automation, rye sourced from adjacent Waldeck Farm). Added a new kentucky-artisan-distillery row for bottlerSlug (see below). Founders are reported elsewhere (Leonid Yangarber, Steve Thompson, Ludwig Vanneron per secondary sources) but I could not open a page naming them directly this session, so owner is left blank. 100% Kentucky straight rye, no peat used.

MAJOR CORRECTION: Fauconnier is real and has a working official site (fauconnier.com, opened), contradicting the seed's 'no web presence found' (its searches evidently missed the exact domain). Founded 1829 in Hesdin/Marconne, Hauts-de-France; a spirits blender/bottler (whiskies, vodkas, rums, gins) that both bottles its own branded products and produces private-label spirits for retailers since 1963; part of La Martiniquaise Group since 2011 (confirmed via la-martiniquaise.com, opened, which lists Fauconnier among its establishments alongside Label 5 and Sir Edward's). Corrected kind from blend to bottler (it is an independent blending/bottling company producing several house brands, not one specific blend) and countryCode from empty to FR. The site does not name 'Highland's Friends', 'Hunting Lodge' or 'O'Brian' specifically, so those remain unconfirmed sub-brands of a now-confirmed real bottler; no peat evidence found anywhere.

Confirmed via Wikipedia (opened): Ian Macleod Distillers (then trading as Russell Brokers/Ian MacLeod & Co) acquired Isle of Skye Blended Whisky in May 1963. No blend composition or peat details found anywhere; kept unknown per the seed's reasoning - the Talisker/Skye heritage marketing evokes but does not state the actual composition.

column7: Morrison Scotch Whisky Distillers (formerly Morrison & Mackay)
column15: Confirmed via the brand's own official site (opened): owned/operated by Morrison Scotch Whisky Distillers, 'solely owned and operated by ... Jamie and Brian Morrison' (the company traded as Morrison & Mackay until 2020). Set bottlerSlug=morrison-mackay, a live producer slug. Corrected defaultTypeName from blend to malt: the official page calls it a 'Blended Malt Scotch Whisky' (built around ex-Bourbon-matured Aultmore per secondary sources), i.e. a vatted malt with no grain component, not a grain-inclusive blend. No peat mentioned on the official page; kept none per the seed's reasoning plus Aultmore's own unpeated Speyside house style.

Confirmed via the official site (opened): Oaxacan corn whiskey brand founded by Douglas French (2014), distilled and bottled exclusively by Scorpion Mezcal S.A. de C.V. in Oaxaca, Mexico, imported by Caballeros Inc./Park Street Imports. No peat/smoke mentioned. defaultTypeName kept empty - corn whiskey has no clean match in the closed type list.

Confirmed via Wikipedia (opened): Suntory Global Spirits (a subsidiary of Suntory Beverage & Food, itself a subsidiary of Suntory Holdings) makes Hibiki from Yamazaki, Hakushu and Chita distillery whisky. This remains a low-specificity fallback row for catalogue rows tagged bare 'Suntory' (e.g. Toki, Ao) with no more specific in-name match - Hakushu, Chita and Hibiki are modeled as separate rows since their facts differ. CORRECTED peatProfile from none to unknown: a handful of limited Suntory editions (some Hakushu releases) are peated, so a blanket none on this fallback row risked stripping a real peat tag from whichever bare-'Suntory' product happens to be one of those editions.

column7: Sakurao Brewery and Distillery (formerly Chugoku Jozo)
column15: Confirmed via japanhandbook.com (opened): the standard/Kiwami/Premium/9-year range is unpeated (malt sourced from Scotland, grain from Canada, aged/blended/bottled by Sakurao Brewery and Distillery, formerly Chugoku Jozo, in a disused JR railway tunnel near Hiroshima). 'Togouchi Peated' is a distinct, explicitly peated expression - confirmed via the producer's own product page (togouchi.com, opened): 18% peated malted barley sourced from Speyside. Wrote a peat rule for pattern 'peated' (peatProfile=light, given the minority 18% proportion) - see rule.tsv, resolving the seed's forward reference to it.

Confirmed via the official site (opened, this session - the seed's own fetch is now re-verified): Lovingston, VA, in the Blue Ridge Mountains; 'the most awarded single malt whisky distillery in America'. 'Courage & Conviction' is confirmed as a distinct affiliated brand line (its own separate row, parentSlug pointing here, is outside this batch). No peat/smoke mention anywhere on the site.

Confirmed via koreatimes.co.kr (opened): Diageo Korea markets White Horse as 'built around a spirit from the Lagavulin Distillery' with 'a distinctive smoky character' and 'bold smokiness'; the blend also carries Caol Ila and Talisker with Linkwood for balance (~40% malt content per other sources). CORRECTED peat from the seed's light to unknown: this is the strongest evidence found, but the page is a news outlet quoting Diageo Korea, not a page on Diageo's or White Horse's own domain (diageobaracademy.com's White Horse page returned 410 Gone this session), and White Horse itself is not Islay-sited, so per policy it stays unknown. Withheld peat proposal: light-to-medium per the cited article; a reviewer should look for an on-domain Diageo/malts.com source to promote this.

Confirmed via the official site (opened): Red Hook, Brooklyn; whiskey is proofed with limestone mineral water trucked from the Rosendale Mines, NY. The current homepage emphasizes bourbon (Heirloom Bourbon, The Vaults 15 Year); Paradigm Rye (a 2023 release per secondary sources) accounts for the row's rye samples and is not shown on the page content fetched, but is consistent with a range spanning bourbon and rye, so defaultTypeName stays empty. No peat/smoke mentioned. Kind kept as blend: whiskey is mostly sourced from Kentucky/Indiana/Tennessee distillates and married in Brooklyn (an NDP/blending model), though 'Baby Jane' is their first fully in-house-distilled release.

new row for coalition. Crestwood, Kentucky craft/contract distillery; confirmed via distillerytrail.com (opened) as the facility where Coalition Whiskey is distilled, aged and bottled (pre-Prohibition all-copper pot still, zero automation, rye sourced from adjacent Waldeck Farm less than a mile away). Reported elsewhere as co-founded/owned by Steve Thompson, but I could not open a page confirming that detail directly this session, so owner is left blank. defaultTypeName left empty (a contract distillery, range not established). No peat evidence found; kept unknown rather than assumed.
